Synopsis:
    US Treasury Secretary Bessent is publicly pressuring the Bank of Japan to raise rates and support a stronger yen, with markets now pricing in a BOJ hike on Sept 18. Japan's 10-year JGB yields broke 3% for the first time in 30 years. PM Takaichi has not pushed back, as a stronger yen suits her fiscal expansion agenda. However, Tokyo is increasingly ceding monetary policy autonomy to Washington. The article warns this dynamic is unsustainable as US and Japanese interests will diverge over time. Bessent is also subtly trying to reframe Japan's economic agenda away from Takaichi's spending plans toward Abenomics-style deregulation.
